checks.statement: For a cyclic generator g of finite order n >= 2, card{g,g^{-1}} = 2 iff n != 2.
checks.reasoning: The two elements coincide iff g=g^{-1}, equivalently g^2=1. Since g has order n, this occurs iff n divides 2. Under n>=2 this is exactly n=2.
checks.outcome: The written n ne 2 condition is mathematically consistent, conditional on the second base being g. This check did not choose g over the retained s alternative or choose an expansion of the shorthand.

checks.statement: The 2 bis condition i(a)i(b)=1 permits the two distinct elements of Omega to have the same image when the generator has order two.
checks.reasoning: Left multiplication by i(a)^{-1} gives i(b)=i(a)^{-1}. A generator of order two equals its inverse, so the images can coincide while a and b remain distinct in Omega.
checks.outcome: The replacement datum is compatible with the degeneracy at n=2. This is a local identity check, not a proof of the whole classification.
